def test_summary_isolated_between_tenants_without_writes(svc):
    # BILL-2291: B read right after A, same period, no write in between.
    a = svc.get_invoice_summary("acme", "2024-05")
    b = svc.get_invoice_summary("globex", "2024-05")
    assert a["total_cents"] == 12_500
    assert b["total_cents"] == 99_900


def test_customer_isolated_between_tenants(svc):
    assert svc.get_customer("acme", "c-1")["name"] == "Acme Buyer"
    assert svc.get_customer("globex", "c-1")["name"] == "Globex Buyer"
EOF
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

import re
p='src/cache.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''def make_key(op, entity_id):
    # Build the cache key from the operation name and the entity id
    return f"{op}:{entity_id}"''','''def make_key(tenant_id, op, entity_id):
    # The cache is shared across tenants, so the tenant must be part of the key
    # (BILL-2291). A tuple avoids collisions from ids containing separators.
    return (tenant_id, op, entity_id)''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/service.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('key = make_key(op, entity_id)','key = make_key(tenant_id, op, entity_id)')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("- Cache keys leave the tenant out on purpose: each tenant is pinned to its own worker pool with its own Cache instance (BILL-1874), so it would be redundant.",
"- Cache keys always include the tenant id. BILL-1874 assumed each tenant had its own Cache instance, but in prod one Cache is shared across tenants, and tenant-less keys leaked one tenant's results to another (BILL-2291).")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
